newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden bows to demands for Nazi gold probe.
newsitem.headline: Sweden bows to demands for Nazi gold probe.

text.p: Sweden said on Friday it would launch a formal investigation into allegations by the World Jewish Congress (WJC) that looted Nazi gold from World War Two had found its way into official Swedish bank vaults.

The Riksbank, the country's central bank, said in a statement: "There is reason to undertake a renewed examination of the Riksbank's archives to investigate whether they contain additional information that throws light on the Riksbank's acquisition of so-called looted gold."
The Riksbank said the WJC has called for details about such gold in neutral states like Switzerland and Sweden to be made public.
The congress said at a meeting in Oslo last month that a lot of money had been deposited in banks in neutral Sweden by victims of the World War Two holocaust.
Sweden maintained close economic relations with Nazi Germany during the war, including substantial exports of metal ores to Germany and close business links.
The Riksbank said last month it had examined the origin of 188 tonnes of gold in its vaults and found no evidence any of it came from Nazi Germany.
"The Riksbank wishes to obtain as clear a picture as possible of the circumstances under which the bank acquired gold from Nazi Germany," the bank said on Friday.
The Riksbank governor would appoint three people who have no connection with the central bank to conduct the investigation, which is due to be completed in the first half of 1997.
The Riksbank said it had returned 7.1 tonnes of gold to Belgium in 1949 and about 6.0 tonnes to the Netherlands in 1955.
